We choose the text-to-SQL task to test LLMs' ability to handle novel interpretations because of its relevance to real-world applications... We create MAGNIFICO by modifying and re-tasking examples from an existing text-to-SQL benchmark, Spider.
We choose the text-to-SQL task to test LLMs' ability to handle novel interpretations because of its relevance to real-world applications.

We use a metric called Relative Performance to measure the generalization ability of models towards acquiring novel interpretations. Our metric provides a measure that is relative to the performance of the model on the corresponding base examples: Relative Performance = min(EX NI / EX base , 1) × 100 where EX NI is the execution accuracy on the examples with novel interpretations from MAG-NIFICO and EX base is the execution accuracy on the corresponding base examples.

The metric for evaluating the generated SQL queries in text2SQL benchmarks is execution accuracy... We use a metric called Relative Performance which is derived from execution accuracy on novel‑interpretation examples and base examples.
The metric for evaluating the generated SQL queries in text2SQL benchmarks is execution accuracy, which compares the output of the execution of the generated query with the ground truth.
